# Quickstart - Set Up Your First Assistant

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

(warning)

## Twilio Alpha - Developer Preview

AI Assistants is a [Twilio Alpha(link takes you to an external page)](https://twilioalpha.com/ "Twilio Alpha") project that's in **Developer Preview**.

View the [current limitations](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/pricing-and-limits "current limitations") for details about feature limits during developer preview.

This Quickstart will guide you through creating your first AI Assistant in the Twilio Console.

An Assistant configuration consists of the following aspects:

- **Base Configuration:** This is where you give your Assistant a name and personality and additional configurations such as connections to [Segment(link takes you to an external page)](https://segment.com/ "Segment").
- **Tools:** Tools enable your Assistant to interact with APIs to solve tasks. For security purposes, Tools are purpose-built webhooks or APIs and shouldn't be general APIs.
- **Knowledge:** Knowledge is a collection of unstructured data (such as knowledge bases) that you want your Assistant to be able to use to answer questions.

Learn more about these core components in the [AI Assistant Overview](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants#core-components "AI Assistant Overview").

At the end of this Quickstart, you'll have an AI Assistant that can answer questions about recent Twilio news using the Twilio blog and about Disney characters using the Disney API.

* * *

## Configure your first Assistant

[configure-your-first-assistant page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/quickstart#configure-your-first-assistant)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Navigate to the [Twilio Console(link takes you to an external page)](https://console.twilio.com/us1/develop/ai-assistants/assistants "Twilio Console") and choose to create a new Assistant. Give it a name that's memorable to you. This name is not used in any customer-facing use cases and is purely for you to identify your Assistant.

Once you've created your Assistant, the first step is to give your Assistant a personality using the Personality Prompt. If you have built with [Large Language Models (LLM)](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-is-a-large-language-model "Large Language Models (LLM)") before, this is similar to a System Prompt but more high-level rather than fixed steps. If you have never worked with an LLM before, think of the Personality Prompt like the context you would give an employee on day one. [Learn more about the Personality Prompt in the AI Assistant overview](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants#base-configuration "Learn more about the Personality Prompt in the AI Assistant overview").

For this Quickstart, use this as an example Personality Prompt:

Copy code block

```

```

Copy this into your configuration and save.

* * *

## Send an initial test message

[send-an-initial-test-message page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/quickstart#send-an-initial-test-message)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Every Assistant comes with a [built-in Simulator](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/simulator "built-in Simulator") that you can use to test your Assistant. To open the Simulator, click **Open Simulator** at the top right of your configuration.

To create a new session in the Simulator in Console, click the **+** button at the top right. Start by entering the identity `email:demo@example.com` (you can change this later when you begin to use Twilio's AI features).

Send a message like "Hello" or ask questions like "What is the best Disney movie?" You haven't connected any Knowledge yet, so any responses are entirely generated by the Assistant's underlying LLM and might be wrong.

* * *

## Upload some Knowledge

[upload-some-knowledge page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/quickstart#upload-some-knowledge)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Right now your Assistant will have some base knowledge from the underlying model but this information might be out of date and your Assistant might end up returning inaccurate information. You can change this by adding a [Knowledge source](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/knowledge "Knowledge source").

Go to the **Knowledge** tab in your Assistant configuration and add a new Knowledge entry. For this example, use the Wikipedia entry on The Walt Disney Company as the Knowledge source. Enter the following configuration details:

| Field | Configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Name | The Walt Disney Company Wikipedia |
| Description | Use this to answer general questions about The Walt Disney Company, including things like its history, company units, leadership, financial data, legacy, and awards. |
| Type | Website |
| URL | `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Walt_Disney_Company` |
| Page Depth | 0 |

When you hit Save, your Assistant will begin crawling the URL provided at the specified page depth for any link in the same domain. This might take a moment, but once the **Status** is marked **Complete**, your Assistant has gathered the relevant information.

Test this new source by going back into the Simulator and asking a specific question like: "How much revenue did The Walt Disney Company make in 2007?" You should see your Assistant ask a question to your new Knowledge source, and once it receives the necessary information, it will craft the response.

Now your Assistant has one Knowledge entry. Next, you'll add the first Tool to your Assistant.

* * *

## Add your first Tool

[add-your-first-tool page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/quickstart#add-your-first-tool)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Knowledge entries are unstructured data sources, whereas [Tools](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/tools "Tools") are how your Assistant can perform HTTP requests for specific tasks. You can use the Tool's description and name to give your Assistant information on when to trigger the Tool.

You can define what the Tool's input should look like with a TypeScript type definition interface, but ultimately the Assistant will decide what input to send, based on the Assistant's interaction with the end user.

This example will use the Disney Characters API as the Assistant's first Tool.

Start by going into the **Tools** section of your Assistant and add a new Tool. Fill out the configuration using the following values:

| Field | Configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Name | Disney Characters |
| Description | Use this tool for information about Disney characters, such as which films or video games they appear in. |
| Input | ```<br>{<br> name: string; // name of the character<br>} <br>``` |
| Method | `GET` |
| URL | `https://api.disneyapi.dev/character?pageSize=2` |

Save this configuration, make sure the toggle for your Tool is on, and go back into the Simulator. Send a message such as: "What Disney games does Moana appear in?"

You should see your Assistant make a request to the new Disney API tool to retrieve the information about your question.

* * *

## Triggering your Assistant using the API

[triggering-your-assistant-using-the-api page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/quickstart#triggering-your-assistant-using-the-api)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Every Assistant comes with a REST API that you can use to trigger a message, rather than using the Simulator. Aside from a request body, you can pass in a SessionId of your choice to maintain and identify the message history and an Identity for the end user.

You will need your Assistant's SID and your Twilio Account SID and Authentication Token to make this request. You can find your Assistant's SID in the Assistant section of the Twilio Console, and find your Account SID and Auth Token from the [Twilio Console homepage(link takes you to an external page)](https://console.twilio.com/ "Twilio Console homepage") under **Account Info**.

Send your first message to your AI Assistant using the following curl example:

```

## What's next?

[whats-next page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/quickstart#whats-next)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Now you've created your first Assistant that can have conversations with users and answer questions about The Walt Disney Company! You can continue exploring by adding more Knowledge sources and Tools to this Assistant, and explore the rest of the Assistant documentation to learn more about what you can build.

- Read about all the [configuring your Assistant](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants#base-configuration "configuring your Assistant")
- Learn more about [Tools](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/tools "Tools")
- Learn more about [Knowledge](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/knowledge "Knowledge")
- Connect your Assistant to a [phone number](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/channels "phone number")
- Enable [Customer Memory](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/customer-memory "Customer Memory") to enable "customer memory" capabilities
- Start collecting human feedback with the [Feedback API](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/guides/feedback "Feedback API")

# Simulator

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

The Simulator allows you to interact with your AI Assistant via the Twilio Console for testing, demo, and debugging purposes. You can find the Simulator at the top right of your Assistant Configuration screen in the Console.

You can define an identity and create a new Simulator session to chat with your Assistant. The view will also show you the output of the Tools and Knowledge the Assistant uses. Each new Simulator session starts a new conversation history.

If you want your Simulator session to make use of either Customer Memory engine, the identity field must match the form: `type:value`, and the `type` field must correlate with an identifier on the profile within Segment. Learn more about identity resolution in the [Segment Unify documentation(link takes you to an external page)](https://segment.com/docs/unify/identity-resolution/identity-resolution-onboarding/ "Segment Unify documentation").

For example:

```

You can use the Simulator to test a wide range of queries, including edge cases, to evaluate the Assistant's responses and adaptability, and to simulate different user personas and scenarios.

# Tools

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

Tools in the Twilio AI Assistant framework are specialized APIs that enable your Assistant to perform specific tasks, such as retrieving real-time data, processing orders, or executing complex operations.

Unlike [Knowledge](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/knowledge "Knowledge"), which provides unstructured data for context and information retrieval, Tools are designed to perform actionable tasks that help the Assistant solve targeted problems. Each Tool is purpose-built, and the Assistant selects the most appropriate Tool based on the user's request.

Tools function similarly to webhooks: when a user makes a specific request, the Assistant triggers the appropriate Tool, which then performs an API call to the relevant service. The Assistant processes the response and delivers it to the user in a conversational manner.

* * *

## Configure Tools

[configure-tools page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/tools#configure-tools)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Configuring Tools for your AI Assistant involves setting up several attributes that define how the Tool interacts with external APIs.

### Tool attributes

[tool-attributes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/tools#tool-attributes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

| Attribute name | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name | A unique identifier for your Tool within the Twilio Console. | Weather Check |
| Description | A brief explanation of the Tool's purpose and function. This description helps the Assistant determine when to use the Tool. | Fetches the current weather information based on the provided location |
| HTTP method | Whether the API request should be an HTTP `GET` or `POST` request. Any response returned from the HTTP endpoint feeds back into the model. For example, you could return plain text from your Tool that provides further instructions for the model: "Tell the user this resource isn't available". | `GET` |
| Webhook URL | The endpoint URL for the request. This URL handles the business logic and interacts with the external API. | `https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast` |
| Input schema | The parameters required for the Tool to function. These parameters, often derived from user input, are passed to the Tool's API endpoint. The schema format is similar to [TypeScript types(link takes you to an external page)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/objects.html "TypeScript types"). Note that the full input schema definition is available to the model, including the comments. | `export type Data = {latitude: number; longitude: number;}` |
| Requires User Verification | Indicates whether customer verification is required (with Twilio Verify) before the Assistant can use the Tool. | \[unchecked\] |
| Authorization Provider | One of: `Basic Auth`, `Auth Token`, `OAuth2.0 Password Grant`, `Custom Auth Header`. What type of authorization the API request requires, and the relevant values if specified. | `Basic Auth` |

Get request input schema

- Input schema is passed automatically as URL parameters. For example if the input schema includes "current\_date" then the webhook URL will include "?current\_date=2025-05-01"

Post request input schema

- Input schema is passed in the body of the message, not in the URL

(warning)

## Warning

AI Assistants is currently not following any HTTP redirects that your Webhook URL might return. This means that if your Webhook URL originally returns an HTTP status code of 301, 302, 307, or 308 with a different URL to visit instead, AI Assistants will not visit the subsequent URL. As an example: The URL `https://twilio.com/` redirects to `https://www.twilio.com/en-us` when you visit it in the browser. AI Assistants currently does not follow such a behavior and so `https://twilio.com/` would not be a valid Webhook URL and instead you would need to use `https://www.twilio.com/en-us` directly.

* * *

## Security and authentication

[security-and-authentication page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/tools#security-and-authentication)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

(information)

## Info

For added security and flexibility, Twilio recommends creating a proxy API endpoint to handle sensitive credentials, which the Assistant can access instead of directly interacting with external APIs. You can do this using Twilio Functions, which lets you host Node.js code directly within Twilio. [Check out sample Tools built for Twilio Functions(link takes you to an external page)](https://github.com/twilio-labs/ai-assistants-samples/tree/main/functions/tools "Check out sample Tools built for Twilio Functions").

Implement security measures to ensure your Tool interacts safely with external services:

- **Authentication**: Out of the box, Tools support various auth methods, including OAuth 2.0 and Basic Authentication.
- **Request validation**: Use the X-Twilio-Signature header to [validate that requests are coming from Twilio](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/security#validating-requests "validate that requests are coming from Twilio").
- **Input validation**: Define input schemas that the AI will automatically validate before making API requests, ensuring that all inputs conform to the expected structure.
- **Data minimization**: Think of your LLM as an untrusted client application: ensure your Tool API only returns data that you're comfortable displaying to the end user. Keeping the amount of data returned from the Tool to a minimum will also improve latency.
- **HTTP headers**: With every HTTP request we will automatically pass the following information as HTTP headers to the request. The AI cannot manipulate these and therefore you can use them to implement access controls to limit on whose behalf the AI can perform actions.

| Name | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `X-Session-Id` | The session ID of your conversation. You can use this for example to identify if the Assistant called the same Tool multiple times from the same conversation. |  |
| `X-Identity` | Used to validate the user's identity and correlates to the Segment identity used for Customer Memory. If you use the Assistant Simulator, this value will be the same as what you put into the User Identity field. | `email:demo@example.com` |
| `X-Twilio-Signature` | A Twilio request signature that you can use to [validate the request came from Twilio](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/security#validating-requests "validate the request came from Twilio"). |  |

* * *

## Use cases

[use-cases page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/alpha/ai-assistants/tools#use-cases)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

You can use Tools in various scenarios to enhance the capabilities of your AI Assistant:

1. **Dynamic real-time information retrieval**: For example, a Tool can fetch weather updates, stock prices, or news headlines from external APIs.
2. **Operations**: Tools can handle tasks such as booking a service, placing an order, or updating a customer record.
3. **Calculations**: Use Tools to execute complex calculations, unit conversions, or generate financial estimates by interfacing with specialized APIs.

# Adding New Projects to your Invoice

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

(information)

## Info

To add a new project to your invoice, you should already have invoicing set up for your Twilio account(s). If you're interested in learning about setting up invoicing for your account, please [contact our Sales team(link takes you to an external page)](https://www.twilio.com/help/sales "contact our Sales team").

* * *

## The Admin Center

[the-admin-center page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/enterprise/add-projects-to-invoice#the-admin-center)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

You'll need to use the Admin Center to create a new Project and add the Project to your existing invoice. You can access the Admin Center by [signing into your Twilio account(link takes you to an external page)](https://www.twilio.com/login "signing into your Twilio account") and clicking on the dropdown in the top right corner of the Twilio Console. In order to access the Admin Center, you'll need to be an Organization admin.

![Twilio PROD Contact Center Dashboard with Admin Center highlighted.](https://www.twilio.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdocs-resources.prod.twilio.com%2F69038b114a4b988407a6470f87b5b088596213d9d0b8055f0f3cbc05efa71587.png&w=3840&q=75)Expand image

### What is an Organization?

[what-is-an-organization page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/enterprise/add-projects-to-invoice#what-is-an-organization)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

A Twilio Organization contains all of your company's Twilio Projects. You can use the Organization to manage separate Projects in a centralized place. You'll manage your Organization within the Admin Center.

Now that you know about the Admin Center and Organizations, you're ready to create a new project and add it to your invoicing.

**Step 1** \- Inside the Admin Center, create an additional Project in your Organization by clicking the "+" icon.

![Admin Center interface showing Projects list with a highlighted 'Create Project' button.](https://www.twilio.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdocs-resources.prod.twilio.com%2Ff58bfba565791c26ee27420642889c539bc91abf467b4971e5fc40a7313e0836.png&w=3840&q=75)Expand image

**Step 2** \- Set a friendly name for your Project ( [this can be changed later).(link takes you to an external page)](https://www.twilio.com/console/project/settings "this can be changed later).") Indicate if this is a Flex Project.

![Create new project form with fields for friendly name and Flex project option.](https://www.twilio.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdocs-resources.prod.twilio.com%2Ffa2ba67201336eaab458d45fcc8db2f066b29d20b7a6e4cdb2caac64d153631f.png&w=3840&q=75)Expand image

**Step 3** \- Your new Project is now a part of your Organization. Your Account Manager will add the new Project to your existing invoice.

# 10001: Account is not active

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 10001

[error-10001 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/10001#error-10001)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/10001#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

This account has been disabled and may not be used until it is reactivated.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/10001#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Lack of funds
- Violation of the Terms of Service or Acceptable Use Policy

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/10001#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Check your account balance. Refill funds if necessary.
- Please reach out to Twilio Support through the [Console(link takes you to an external page)](https://console.twilio.com/ "Console") or [Help Center(link takes you to an external page)](https://support.twilio.com/ "Help Center").

# 10002: Trial accounts do not support the feature you tried to use

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 10002

[error-10002 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/10002#error-10002)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PHONE NUMBERS

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/10002#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Premium features are limited to full accounts, so you must upgrade your account if you wish to use them.

For guidance on updating your account, please see [How to Work with your Free Twilio Trial Account](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/tutorials/how-to-use-your-free-trial-account#how-to-upgrade-your-account "How to Work with your Free Twilio Trial Account").

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/10002#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

You attempted to use a premium feature with a trial account.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/10002#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Upgrade to a full account and try the feature again.

# 11200: HTTP retrieval failure

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 11200

[error-11200 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11200#error-11200)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11200#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

We try to provide specific webhook errors whenever possible, however in this instance we are unable to identify the exact cause of the webhook delivery/response issue. To prevent 11200 errors, ensure that your webhook receiving infrastructure can quickly respond to inbound Twilio requests with a 2xx status code.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11200#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Web server returned a 4xx or 5xx HTTP response to Twilio
- Network disruptions between Twilio and your web server; these can be within your or Twilio's infrastructure or wider disruptions to the internet at large.
- Firewalls (network or application level) between Twilio and your infrastructure
- Misconfigured Web Server
- No Content-Type header attached to response
- Content-Type doesn't match actual content, e.g. an MP3 file that is being served with Content-Type: audio/x-wav, instead of Content-Type: audio/mpeg

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11200#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Double check that your TwiML URL does not return a 4xx or 5xx error
- Make certain that the URL does not perform a 302 redirect to an invalid URL
- Confirm the URL requested is not protected by HTTP Auth
- Make sure your web server allows HTTP POST requests to static resources (if the URL refers to .xml or .html files)
- Verify your web server is up and responsive
- Check to see that the URL host is not a private or local IP address
- Verify the ping times and packet loss between your web server and api.twilio.com
- Review firewall rules; modern web application firewalls can trigger on only a small subset of inbound connections leading to inconsistent behavior.
- Check logs at the very edge of your infrastructure to verify if TCP connection attempts are arriving at your edge. If you have confirmed these requests are not reaching your infrastructure, please reach out to [support(link takes you to an external page)](https://www.twilio.com/console/support/tickets/create "support").
- Use more robust options for webhook receipt. For inbound messages and calls be sure to provide a fallback URL (ideally on separate infrastructure). Transition integrations to [Event Streams](https://www.twilio.com/docs/events "Event Streams") which has various event sink types including webhooks with built in retries.
- Review your use of any [webhook connection overrides](https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/webhooks/webhooks-connection-overrides "webhook connection overrides"). In general the defaults provide the best results, start by reconfiguring your webhook URL without any fragment overrides and see if the problem persists.
- If synchronously processing a webhook requires significant time, we recommend that you simply acknowledge the event by quickly responding with an empty 202 (Accepted) and then processing the message on your own timeline. Replies to inbound message events can be done at any time by making a call to the REST API.

* * *

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

### TCP connection timed out

[tcp-connection-timed-out page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11201#tcp-connection-timed-out)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Twilio cannot establish a TCP connection to your web server. The two attempts to connect to your web server were timed out. Each connection attempt has a 5 second timeout.

- network outage between Twilio and your web server

#### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11201#possible-solutions)

- verify firewall configuration in your network or on the web server
- verify network connectivity to your web server
- verify the HTTP URL provided is accessible to the public Internet

# 11205: HTTP connection failure

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 11205

[error-11205 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11205#error-11205)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11205#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

### HTTP connection failure

[http-connection-failure page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11205#http-connection-failure)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

There was a network failure attempting to connect to this URL. Twilio will try for 10 seconds to establish a TCP connection to your URL (two 5-second attempts). Twilio will wait for a total of 15 seconds to receive an HTTP response. This includes the TCP connection time, so if it took six seconds to establish a TCP connection, your server would have 9 seconds to deliver an HTTP response. If either of those timers expire, we fail the request, fire a notification, and try your fallback URL, if one is specified.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11205#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Network outages between Twilio and your web server.
- URLs that reference private IP addresses or localhost.
- Twilio's TCP timeout is 10 seconds. If you see an error in Request Inspector after more than 10000 milliseconds, Twilio could locate your server, but could not establish a TCP connection with it.
- Twilio's HTTP timeout is 15 seconds. If you see an error in Request Inspector returned after more than 15000 milliseconds, Twilio was able to establish a TCP connection with your server, but the HTTP response from the server failed.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11205#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Verify the URL provided is accessible to the public internet.
- Verify network connectivity to your web server.
- Check your TCP logs to verify inbound connection attempts are successful.
- Check HTTP server logs to verify a response was generated and returned within the timeout.
- Check your edge element logs to verify responses are making it out of your infrastructure.

# 11206: HTTP protocol violation

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 11206

[error-11206 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11206#error-11206)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE MESSAGING

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11206#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

There was an error speaking HTTP to the target URL.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11206#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Server misconfiguration
- Network disruption
- Making HTTP connections to an HTTPS port
- There is an invalid symbol in the TwiML Cookie

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11206#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Verify your web server is serving valid HTTP for the URL
- Verify the network connection to your server is stable
- Verify the URL is not directing you to an SSL port
- Remove the following characters from the TwiML Cookies: '\\t', '\\r', '\\n', '\\v', '\\f'
- TwiML cookies cannot have an empty name

# 11216: HTTP invalid redirect

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 11216

[error-11216 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11216#error-11216)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11216#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Twilio sent a webhook to your server and your server responded with a 3xx status code that was not a valid redirect.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11216#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Your server responded with an non-redirect HTTP status code in the 3xx series. Twilio will only follow redirects for status codes 301, 302, 303, and 307.
- Your server did not include a location header in the redirect response

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11216#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Update your webhook configuration specifying the final URL you would like to be called, removing the need for redirects.
- Ensure you are using a standard redirect HTTP status code (301, 302, 303, or 307)
- Ensure that you are including a valid url in the location header of your response.

# 11217: HTTP error response code

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 11217

[error-11217 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11217#error-11217)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11217#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Twilio sent a webhook to your server and your server responded with a 4xx or 5xx status code.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11217#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- There was an error in your server (500).
- There was a problem between your proxy and your server (502, 503, 504).
- The URL specified in your webhook configuration is incorrect (404, 410).
- Your server is attempting to rate limit Twilio's webhook requests (429). Twilio's webhooks do not support rate limiting.
- Your webhook configuration does not have appropriate permissions to call the configured URL (403).

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11217#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Review the configured webhook URL to ensure that it is correct.
- Look for and fix errors in your server logs.
- Ensure that you can get 2xx status codes by calling your webhook URL.
- Review your proxy and authentication configurations.
- For rate limiting issues, consider shifting to Event Streams HTTP Sink which [support rate limiting](https://www.twilio.com/docs/events/faq/problems-on-delivery#what-does-throttle-sink-means-for-eventstreams "support rate limiting").

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11220#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

During SSL/TLS negotiation, Twilio experienced a connection reset.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11220#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Incompatible cipher suites in use by the client and the server. This would require the client to use (or enable) a cipher suite that is supported by the server.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11220#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Verify cipher suites in-use are up to date. Twilio-supported ciphers can be found [here(link takes you to an external page)](https://support.twilio.com/hc/en-us/articles/360007724794-Notice-Twilio-REST-API-s-TLS-and-Cipher-Suite-Security-Changes-for-June-2019 "here")
- Use compatible version of TLS, Twilio supports TLS 1.2.

# 11237: Certificate Invalid - Could not find path to certificate

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 11237

[error-11237 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11237#error-11237)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

ERROR

* * *

## Error - 11237

[error---11237 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11237#error---11237)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

### Certificate Invalid - Could not find path to certificate

[certificate-invalid---could-not-find-path-to-certificate page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11237#certificate-invalid---could-not-find-path-to-certificate)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Twilio tried to validate your SSL certificate but was unable to find it in our certificate store.

#### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11237#possible-causes)

- You are using a self signed certificate.
- The certificate authority you are using is not on our list of approved certificate authorities.
- Your certificate chain is incomplete and requires an additional download.

#### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11237#possible-solutions)

- Do not use a self signed certificate.
- Concatenate your certificate chain so that no additional download is required.
- Twilio uses CAs that are approved by Mozilla, you can find the full list [here(link takes you to an external page)](https://ccadb-public.secure.force.com/mozilla/IncludedCACertificateReport "here").
- For testing purposes you can [disable SSL Certificate Validation in Console(link takes you to an external page)](https://www.twilio.com/console/project/settings "disable SSL Certificate Validation in Console").

# 11750: TwiML response body too large

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 11750

[error-11750 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11750#error-11750)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11750#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

## Error - 11750

[error---11750 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11750#error---11750)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

## TwiML response body too large

[twiml-response-body-too-large page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11750#twiml-response-body-too-large)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

In your response to Twilio's request, the response body is larger than 64 kB.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11750#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- The TwiML that you are serving is larger than 64 kB
- You are serving non-TwiML content in your response; e.g. error message output

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11750#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Verify that you are serving TwiML in your response to Twilio's request.
- Verify that you are including this header in your TwiML response: `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>`
- Limit your TwiML response to 64 kB or less.
- Does your TwiML include the [Play verb](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/twiml/play "Play verb")? Double-check the encoding and MIME type to ensure they are supported.
- Check that your TwiML is formatted properly. To quickly verify your TwiML, you can copy and paste it into a new [TwiML bin in the Twilio Console(link takes you to an external page)](https://www.twilio.com/console/runtime/twiml-bins/create "TwiML bin in the Twilio Console").
- Check to see if your application is throwing errors. This may cause your application to send a large debug output back to Twilio instead of the expected TwiML.
- If you are trying to send a `200` response in a status callback, use an empty TwiML response: `<Response/>`

## Error - 11751

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

### Media Message -> Media exceeds messaging provider size limit

[media-message---media-exceeds-messaging-provider-size-limit page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11751#media-message---media-exceeds-messaging-provider-size-limit)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Maximum size limit depends on the messaging channel.

- For an MMS message, the size limit is [5MB](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sms/accepted-mime-types "5MB").
- For a WhatsApp message, the size limit is [16MB](https://www.twilio.com/docs/whatsapp/guidance-whatsapp-media-messages "16MB").

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11751#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The total size of the media message request exceeds the maximum size limit for the channel.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/11751#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

If you are sending multiple media files on a message, split them into multiple requests to reduce the size of each request.

# 12100: Document parse failure

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 12100

[error-12100 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/12100#error-12100)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

ERROR

* * *

## Error - 12100

[error---12100 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/12100#error---12100)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

### Document parse failure

[document-parse-failure page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/12100#document-parse-failure)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Twilio was unable to parse the provided XML Document.

Your TwiML document must be a valid XML Document, or Twilio will not be able to read your document. You can debug XML parsing errors by getting the response body in the [debugger](https://www.twilio.com/user/account/debugger "debugger"), and then using an online validation tool like the [W3C Validation Service(link takes you to an external page)](http://validator.w3.org/#validate_by_input "W3C Validation Service").

#### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/12100#possible-causes)

- There is a leading space, or an empty line, before the XML type header (i.e. `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>`)
- The root `<Response>` element is missing
- There is an unclosed element
- There is an unquoted attribute
- There is an improperly nested element

#### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/12100#possible-solutions)

- Make sure there is no extra space or line at the beginning of the file before the type header
- Make sure your root element is <Response>
- XML is case sensitive, make sure your start and end elements match case. (Twilio elements begin with a capital letter)
- Make sure characters such as < > and & are escaped properly, as `< > and &`.

# 12300: Invalid Content-Type

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 12300

[error-12300 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/12300#error-12300)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/12300#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Twilio is unable to process the Content-Type of the provided URL. Please see Twilio's [documentation on accepted content types](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/twiml#twilio-understands-mime-types "documentation on accepted content types ") for more information on valid Content-Types.

You must return a Content-Type for all requests. Requests without a Content-Type will appear in the [Debugger](https://www.twilio.com/console/runtime/debugger "Debugger") as a 502 Bad Gateway error.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/12300#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Having a phone number, outgoing call request or action attribute refer to a non-XML or audio resource.
- Having a Play verb attempt to play non-audio content, such as XML or text.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/12300#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Verify that that your web server is returning a Content-Type and it is the expected value
- Make sure the URL noted refers to a valid resource
- Make sure messages to or from your Twilio phone number are using a supported content-type. See the [full list of supported content types](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sms/accepted-mime-types "full list of supported content types").
- Use one of the [supported request types](https://www.twilio.com/docs/runtime/functions/request-flow#supported-requests "supported request types") to call a Twilio function.

# 13214: Dial: Invalid callerId value

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## WARNING: 13214

[warning-13214 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13214#warning-13214)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

WARNING

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13214#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

## Warning - 13214

[warning---13214 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13214#warning---13214)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

### Dial: Invalid callerId value

[dial-invalid-callerid-value page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13214#dial-invalid-callerid-value)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

callerId must be the calling number, called number, or a validated outgoing number. Additionally, if the calling leg is a client leg, the caller ID is required and must be a validated outgoing number. See the [Dial Verb](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/twiml/dial#callerId "Dial Verb") API Reference for more information.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13214#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Carriers may send invalid Caller IDs on Incoming calls to Twilio. If a specific Caller ID is not explicitly defined on the verb, the invalid Caller ID will be passed to the destination. This may cause some destination providers to reject the call, and Twilio will mark it as failed.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13214#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

To work around this, your application should recognize invalid caller IDs, and substitute them with a valid Caller ID to construct the subsequent .

# 13222: Dial->Number: Invalid sendDigits value

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## WARNING: 13222

[warning-13222 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13222#warning-13222)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

WARNING

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13222#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The `sendDigits` attribute may contain numbers, the `#` and `*` characters, the letters `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, as well as lowercase `w` to "wait" for half a second or uppercase `W` to "wait" for a full second. See the [Dial Verb](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/twiml/dial "Dial Verb") API Reference for more information.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13222#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The attribute `sendDigits` includes an invalid character.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13222#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Ensure the `sendDigits` attribute only contains the characters: `0123456789ABCD*#wW`.

# 13223: Dial: Invalid phone number format

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## WARNING: 13223

[warning-13223 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13223#warning-13223)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

WARNING

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13223#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Phone Numbers must be in E.164 format. E.164 numbers are formatted \[+\] \[country code\] \[subscriber number including area code\] and can have a maximum of 15 digits.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13223#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- The phone number you are attempting to dial is not in E.164 format
- The `<Number>` noun inside your `<Dial>` TwiML instructions is not present
- You are attempting to dial something that is not a phone number

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13223#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Check the format of the phone number inside your `<Dial><Number>` TwiML.

Verify that the number is in [E.164 format](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-e164 "E.164 format"):

- Includes the country code
- Includes the area code
- Does not exceed 15 digits
- Does not include any invalid characters, like hyphens or parentheses

In your TwiML instructions, the phone number must be between the opening and closing `<Number>` tags, which are nested within `<Dial>`'s opening and closing tags:

Copy code block

```

```

If you are attempting to `<Dial>` an SDK end-user, ensure you're using the `<Client>` noun inside your `<Dial>` tags.

If you are attempting to `<Dial>` a SIP endpoint, ensure you're using the `<Sip>` noun inside your `<Dial>` tags.

For more information, read the [`<Dial>` docs](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/twiml/dial).

Copy code block

# 13224: Dial: Twilio does not support calling this number or the number is invalid

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 13224

[error-13224 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13224#error-13224)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13224#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Twilio does not support calling this number or the number is invalid

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13224#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

This error occurs when the provided number is not in E.164 format; for example using local dialing pattern 01234567890 instead of the full E.164 address +441234567890. This can also occur when calls are attempted to non-existent country codes, area codes, or exchanges. For example, there is no +693 country code, no +1238 US area code, and no 555 US exchange.

This can also occur with properly-formatted, valid destinations if none of Twilio's carrier partners are able to deliver the call; for example due to a telecom network outage in the phone number's local area.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13224#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Use E.164 formatting and ensure the destination is a valid, in-service destination.

# 13225: Dial: Call blocked by Twilio

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 13225

[error-13225 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13225#error-13225)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13225#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The destination number is blocked by Twilio.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13225#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The outbound call to the destination number was blocked by Twilio. Potential causes may be:

- The destination has a high-risk of fraud
- Due to regulatory reasons, the destination cannot be reached
- You are placing a call to a +1 destination and your account is missing a Primary Customer Profile

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13225#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Potential solutions may be:

- If your destination is being incorrectly identified as high-risk of fraud and you have a legitimate need to call this number, please reach out to Twilio Support through the [Console(link takes you to an external page)](https://console.twilio.com/ "Console") or [Help Center(link takes you to an external page)](https://support.twilio.com/hc/en-us "Help Center").
- If you are placing a call to a +1 destination and your account is missing a Primary Customer Profile, create one in [TrustHub(link takes you to an external page)](https://console.twilio.com/us1/account/trust-hub/customer-profiles "TrustHub").

# 13227: Geo Permission configuration is not permitting call

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 13227

[error-13227 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13227#error-13227)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13227#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

You attempted to initiate an outbound phone call to a phone number that is not enabled on your account.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13227#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

User dialed a destination your application is not enabled to support calling to.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13227#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Please check your [Voice Dialing Geographic Permissions(link takes you to an external page)](https://www.twilio.com/console/voice/calls/geo-permissions "Voice Dialing Geographic Permissions"), fix it, and try again.

# 13238: Dial->Conference: Invalid Verb used in waitUrl, holdUrl, or announceUrl TwiML

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 13238

[error-13238 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13238#error-13238)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13238#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The TwiML that executes via the waitUrl, holdUrl, or announceUrl can only contain Say, Play, Pause, and Redirect verbs. Dial, Gather, Hangup and Record are not allowed.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13238#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Dial, Gather, Hangup or Record verbs are used in the TwiML.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13238#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Remove Dial, Gather, Hangup and Record verbs from the TwiML.

reCAPTCHA

Recaptcha requires verification.

### Dial->Conference: Invalid Trim Value

[dial-conference-invalid-trim-value page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13239#dial-conference-invalid-trim-value)

# 13247: Dial: Invalid From number (caller ID)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 13247

[error-13247 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13247#error-13247)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13247#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

You attempted to initiate an outbound phone call or message, but the `From` parameter you supplied was not a valid phone number or alphanumeric sender ID.

Twilio accepts phone numbers in [E.164 format](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-e164 "E.164 format") (i.e. "+1 format"), 10-digit US and Canadian numbers with any combination of non-digit separators, or Alphanumeric Sender IDs (SMS only) with up to 11 alphanumeric characters \[a-zA-Z0-9\]. Refer to [this page(link takes you to an external page)](https://support.twilio.com/hc/en-us/articles/223133867-Using-Alphanumeric-Sender-ID-with-Messaging-Services "this page") for acceptable characters.

The number must not be on a do-not-originate (DNO) list, and Alpha Sender IDs may not be generic.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13247#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- You have supplied a phone number that was not in [E.164 format](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-e164 "E.164 format")
- Your `From` phone number is on a do-not-originate (DNO) list

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13247#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Ensure your number is formatted in [E.164 format](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-e164 "E.164 format")
- Ensure that your `From` number is assigned and not on a do-not-originate (DNO) list.

reCAPTCHA

Recaptcha requires verification.

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

### Gather->Play: Invalid Content-Type

[gather-play-invalid-content-type page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13325#gather-play-invalid-content-type)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Play requires an audio Content-Type

#### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13325#possible-causes)

- Play references a URL that does not return audio or is returning an invalid Content-Type.

#### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13325#possible-solutions)

- Make certain the URL returns an audio file
- See the [Play Verb](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/twiml/play "Play Verb") API Reference for more information on valid Content-Types.

# 13430: Play: Invalid DTMF String

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## WARNING: 13430

[warning-13430 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13430#warning-13430)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

WARNING

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13430#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The `digit` attribute may contain numbers, the `#` and `*` characters, the letters `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, as well as lowercase `w` to "wait" for half a second or uppercase `W` to "wait" for a full second.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13430#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The attribute `digit` includes an invalid character.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13430#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Ensure the `digit` attribute only contains the characters: `0123456789ABCD*#wW`.

# 13521: \`<Say>\` element character limits exceeded

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## WARNING: 13521

[warning-13521 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13521#warning-13521)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

WARNING

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13521#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The maximum text length inside a verb is limited and varies depending on the option used. Basic, Polly and Google TTS have different limits and character count.

See the [Say Verb](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/twiml/say#voice "Say Verb") API Reference for more information.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13521#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The maximum text length inside the `<Say>` verb has been exceeded.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13521#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Make sure that the character limit is under the limit for the TTS type being used:

- Basic TTS Voices are limited to 4096 UTF-8 single byte characters
- Polly TTS Voices are limited to 3000 UTF-8 single byte characters; note that SSML tags do not contribute to the character count
- Google TTS Voices are limited to 5000 UTF-8 single byte characters; note that SSML tags, newlines and spaces contribute to the character count
- The URL-encoded string cannot exceed 4500 characters

[warning---13615 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13615#warning---13615)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

### Record: transcribeCallback URL is invalid

[record-transcribecallback-url-is-invalid page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13615#record-transcribecallback-url-is-invalid)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The transcribeCallback URL provided in the `<Record>` verb is not valid.

#### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13615#possible-solutions)

Make sure you submit a fully qualified URL including:

- protocol (http:// or https://)
- hostname
- file path
- properly url-encoded query parameters

Twilio must be able to reach this URL over the public Internet.

# 13617: Record: Recording length is out of range for transcription

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## WARNING: 13617

[warning-13617 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13617#warning-13617)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

WARNING

* * *

## Warning - 13617

[warning---13617 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13617#warning---13617)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

### Record: Recording length is out of range for transcription

[record-recording-length-is-out-of-range-for-transcription page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13617#record-recording-length-is-out-of-range-for-transcription)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Twilio could not process the transcription because the duration of the recording is either too short or too long. The recording itself will not be affected.

#### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13617#possible-solutions)

- Transcription is currently limited to recordings with a duration greater than 2 seconds and less than 120 seconds. Consider using the maxLength parameter for `<Record>` to limit the duration of the recording. See [transcription TwiML reference](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/twiml/record#attributes-transcribe "transcription TwiML reference") for more information.

# 13618: Record: Recording not available for transcription

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## WARNING: 13618

[warning-13618 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13618#warning-13618)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

WARNING

* * *

## Warning - 13618

[warning---13618 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13618#warning---13618)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

### Record: Recording not available for transcription

[record-recording-not-available-for-transcription page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13618#record-recording-not-available-for-transcription)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

#### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13618#possible-causes)

- The recording was deleted before before Twilio was able to fetch the recording for transcription.

#### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13618#possible-solutions)

- Make a request to delete the recording once you receive the transcribe callback instead of the record callback. This ensures that the recording is available for Twilio to transcribe and still allows you to delete recordings from Twilio.

# 13801: Refer not allowed on non-SIP call legs

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 13801

[error-13801 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13801#error-13801)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13801#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The Refer verb is only allowed on SIP call legs, e.g. you can refer an incoming SIP call that originate from SIP infrastructure or an outbound call to a SIP destination. Calls to or from other destinations, such as a phone number or Twilio Client cannot be referred.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13801#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Your application attempted to invoke the Refer verb on a PSTN or Twilio Client call leg.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13801#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- For more information on understanding what does and does not constitute a SIP call leg, please see [Understanding SIP Call Legs](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/twiml/refer#understanding-call-legs "Understanding SIP Call Legs").
- While invoking Refer on a SIP leg is unique in that it removes Twilio from the call path, the effect of transferring a call to another party can be accomplished on all leg types by simply using the Dial verb to call the other party.

# 13802: Dial: No referUrl attribute specified

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 13802

[error-13802 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13802#error-13802)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13802#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

In order to send a SIP REFER message to an established `<Dial>` call, the `referUrl` attribute must be specified in the TwiML. In this case, a REFER was received on a `<Dial>` call without a `referUrl` attribute present.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13802#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Your `<Dial>` verb did not include a `referUrl` attribute or the attribute was misspelled

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13802#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Add a valid `referUrl` attribute to your `<Dial>` verb
- For more information on sending REFER to Twilio, see [Refer to Twilio](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/api/refer-to-twilio "Refer to Twilio")

# 13807: Client Notification URL Error Response

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 13807

[error-13807 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13807#error-13807)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13807#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The Client Notification URL returned an error.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13807#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Your URL is returning 5xx error due to an internal server issue
- Your URL is returning a 400, 401, or 403 due to a server misconfiguration or authentication/authorization issue
- Your URL returned a 404 due to a misconfiguration of your `clientNotificationUrl` in your TwiML or API request
- Your URL returned a 404 because your application could not find a binding for the user receiving the call

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/13807#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Resolve your server errors
- Reconfigure your `clientNotificationUrl` to the correct URL
- Remove the user who has no binding from your call routing
- Return a 200 OK
- Verify you are using [Client Call Notification Webhook](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/sdks/call-notification-webhook "Client Call Notification Webhook") correctly

# 14107: SMS send rate limit exceeded

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 14107

[error-14107 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14107#error-14107)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE SMS

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14107#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Too many messages have been sent between two numbers within a short time period, possibly indicating a runaway job or infinite loop. There is a limit of 30 outbound replies between two phone numbers in a 30-second period.

A counter is set for each outbound reply in a conversation (between two numbers). When the first reply occurs, the counter starts at 1. If the next reply is sent less than 30 seconds after the prior reply, then the counter goes to 2. This will continue if each reply is less than 30 seconds, until the counter surpasses 30; at this time, Twilio will set any further messages in the loop to "failed" status for 30 seconds, with this error code.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14107#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- repeated rapid responses by the end user (30 replies in less than 30 seconds)
- infinite loop caused by self referencing Sms or Message verb action URL
- infinite loop caused by self referencing Redirect verb URL
- runaway process making repeated outgoing REST API requests

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14107#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- make certain any action or Redirect URL's do not loop back to the same TwiML document.
- make sure you are not inadvertently sending a large quantity of messages to the same phone number, e.g. a script caught in a loop
- if you need this protection disabled for your Twilio Account, [contact Twilio Support(link takes you to an external page)](https://www.twilio.com/console/support/tickets/create "contact Twilio Support"). Please note, if you choose to have this feature disabled, you must have protection in place in your application to prevent costly auto-reply loops.

Recaptcha requires verification.

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## WARNING: 14109

[warning-14109 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14109#warning-14109)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE SMS

WARNING

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14109#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

## Warning - 14109

[warning---14109 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14109#warning---14109)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

### TwiML Reply message limit exceeded

[twiml-reply-message-limit-exceeded page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14109#twiml-reply-message-limit-exceeded)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Too many TwiML reply messages have been sent in response to a single incoming message. You can send a maximum of 10 TwiML replies per incoming message.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14109#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- A runaway loop or other error in your application generated more than 10 TwiML replies to a single incoming message
- You have attempted to send >10 TwiML replies to a single incoming message

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14109#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- If you need to generate >10 outbound messages for one incoming message, please use new API requests to create these messages.

# 14207: Enqueue: The targeted queue reached max queue size

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## WARNING: 14207

[warning-14207 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14207#warning-14207)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

WARNING

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14207#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The targeted queue has reached its maxSize limit. Once the queue reaches the limit, new requests to queue calls using will be rejected.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14207#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

A full queue can indicate higher volume, longer queue times, or an incorrectly configured queue's maxSize.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14207#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

A queue's maxSize can be adjusted to a maximum of 5000. Use the [Queue API](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/api/queue-resource "Queue API") to identify the current maxSize and adjust accordingly.

If a waitUrl is provided for , the parameters MaxQueueSize and CurrentQueueSize are included in the Webhook request to the waitUrl. Your application can use this information to determine queue capacity and adjust max queue size via the [API](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/api/queue-resource "API").

If the queue is already configured for the maximum allowed queue size (5000), one possible workaround is to create multiple queues and distribute the requests between them.

Recaptcha requires verification.

[dial-queue-invalid-whisper-url page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14211#dial-queue-invalid-whisper-url)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The whisper url is invalid.

#### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14211#possible-solutions)

Make sure you submit a fully qualified URL including:

- protocol (http:// or https://)
- hostname
- file path
- properly url-encoded query parameters

Twilio must be able to reach this URL over the public Internet.

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

[warning-14241 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14241#warning-14241)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

TASKROUTER

WARNING

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14241#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Starting Nov. 30, 2021 we will no longer return data older than 30 days, and instead return a 400-response for requests with <start\_date> older than 30 days.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14241#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

<start\_date> is older than 30 days.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/14241#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Pass a <start\_date> that is within 30 days.

# 15002: Call Progress: Queue Timeout

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 15002

[error-15002 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/15002#error-15002)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

ERROR

* * *

## Error - 15002

[error---15002 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/15002#error---15002)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

### Call Progress: Queue Timeout

[call-progress-queue-timeout page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/15002#call-progress-queue-timeout)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

A callback request timed out in the callback queue.

#### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/15002#possible-causes)

- Your application is not responding to Call Progress Events in a timely manner leading to queued callbacks expiring before they are sent.
- There was a network disruption between Twilio and your web server.

#### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/15002#possible-solutions)

- Please ensure your application is responding to callbacks in a timely manner.

# 15003: Call Progress: Warning Response to Callback URL

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## WARNING: 15003

[warning-15003 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/15003#warning-15003)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

WARNING

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/15003#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Got an HTTP warning in response to the callback URL.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/15003#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

- Your application returned a 4xx or 5xx HTTP response to Twilio.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/15003#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Ensure your application responds to callbacks with:

- 200 OK
- Content-Type: text/xml
- Valid TwiML

Or respond with 204 No Content and an empty response body.

# 15004: Action Callback URL must be an absolute URL when using TwiML to update in-progress calls

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 15004

[error-15004 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/15004#error-15004)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/15004#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The TwiML provided for updating the in-progress call must use absolute URL for action callback.

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/15004#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

A relative URL is provided for action callbacks when updating in-progress call with TwiML.

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/15004#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Provide an absolute URL for the action attribute when updating in-progress call with TwiML.

# 16023: Dial->Conference: Invalid participant label, must not exceed 128 characters, must not be a CallSid, must not contain '/'

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

* * *

* * *

## ERROR: 16023

[error-16023 page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/16023#error-16023)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

PROGRAMMABLE VOICE

ERROR

* * *

## Description

[description page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/16023#description)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

The participant label specified in an API call to create a voice conference participant was invalid. It may not exceed 128 characters, it may not be a CallSid, and it may not contain a '/' (even in URL encoded form %2F).

### Possible Causes

[possible-causes page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/16023#possible-causes)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

A POST to conference participants call to the Twilio API specified a participant label which is greater than 128 characters or which resembles a CallSid ("CA" followed by 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters), or contains the '/' character or URL encoded '/' character (%2F).

### Possible Solutions

[possible-solutions page anchor](https://www.twilio.com/docs/api/errors/16023#possible-solutions)

Positive FeedbackNegative Feedback

Shorten the length of the ParticipantLabel parameter, avoid using a call SID and avoid including '/' characters.
